f.cmp_text: At every step count both labs ran from 1 to 50, flow with Euler scores better than all three diffusion samplers. At 4 evaluations it scores FD 158.3 against 478.9 for DDIM and 300.3 for DDPM; at 10, 64.4 against 181.3, 130.5 and DPM-Solver++'s 115.1; at 20, 49.8 against 130.9, 77.9 and 101.2. The midpoint solver does better still: 47.3 with 2 steps (4 evaluations, 1.37 s for 1,000 images) and 45.4 with 5 (10 evaluations); DDPM needs 250 steps to reach 39.7. Plain Heun is the outlier (1,333.2 at 4 evaluations, 470.2 at 10): section 3's endpoint problem. Making its last step Euler fixes it (76.7 at 5 evaluations, 48.1 at 9) and gives the best unguided flow score in the lab, 43.5 at 19 evaluations. Accuracy is high for every flow run from 2 Euler steps (above 85%); what few steps cost is diversity (15.3 at 2 Euler steps, 25.7 at 50, real images 28.9): few-step samples are cleaner, more average garments.
f.ddpm_wins: With many steps the stochastic DDPM sampler reaches FD 34.9 at 1,000 steps (39.7 at 250), below every unguided flow run (best 43.5). Solving the flow ODE more exactly does not help: Euler with 250 steps scores 53.0 and midpoint with 25 steps 53.1, worse than 5 midpoint steps, so the coarse solvers' error happens to improve this under-trained model's samples, as DDPM's fresh noise does (the Diffusion lab saw DDPM beat DDIM for the same reason). A stochastic sampler for the flow model would test that; not run here. With guidance (section 7) the flow model reaches 23.8, the best score in either lab.
f.shift_text: no shift is best at both step counts: at 4 Euler steps FD 158.3 against 294.6 with shift 1/3 and 242.4 with shift 3; at 10 steps 64.4, 90.4 and 82.4. The shift exists because a large image keeps recognisable structure at noise levels that wipe out a small one, so a 1024-pixel model needs more of its steps near the noise end; a 28 × 28 model has nothing to gain.
f.cfg_text: Flow, Euler 50 steps, 1,000 samples measured: FD 48.9 unguided (s = 1), 23.8 at s = 1.5 (class accuracy 94.6%; real images score 18.93), 54.6 at s = 2, 140.5 at s = 3 and 275.7 at s = 5, where accuracy is 99.7% and diversity has fallen from 25.7 to 20.4: guidance trades variety for recognisability, and past a small scale FD punishes the lost variety. s = 0, the unconditional model (it only trained on the 10% of examples whose label was dropped), scores 362.2. The Diffusion lab's DDIM-50 sweep peaked at s = 2 (FD 35.55; it did not try 1.5); the flow model's best is lower.
f.bug_text: Correct sampling: FD 48.9. Integrating from t = 1 down to 0 (diffusers' direction) with this t = 0-is-noise model: FD 1,867.8, class accuracy 10.7% (chance is 10%). Passing t × 1000 (what diffusers' pipelines give a transformer) to a net trained on t in [0, 1]: FD 1,229.3, accuracy 21.3%. Neither raises an error. measured
f.rf_text: After reflow one Euler step scores FD 159.8 (from 1,253.5), two steps 99.5 (from 489.3) and four 83.1 (from 158.3); at 50 steps 73.1 against 48.9 before. One step now lands 0.10 (RMS per pixel) from the 50-step answer, against 0.34 before, and the 50-step paths' straightness rises from 0.986 to 0.999. measured

def cfm_loss(model, x1, y, p_uncond=0.1):
    """Conditional flow matching with straight paths (rectified flow / OT-CFM with sigma_min = 0)."""
    x0 = torch.randn_like(x1)
    t = torch.rand(x1.shape[0], device=x1.device)
    tt = t.view(-1, 1, 1, 1)
    pred = model((1 - tt) * x0 + tt * x1, t, drop_labels(y, p_uncond))
    loss = F.mse_loss(pred, x1 - x0)
    return loss, {"loss": loss.item()}
